objective_statement: find the free input words for which the permutation-with-initial-linear-layer reproduces the target output words exactly; the remaining output words are unconstrained

program.name: Six Worlds of Gröbner Basis Cryptanalysis: Application to Anemoi
program.version: ToSC 2024 no. 4, pp. 138-190, DOI 10.46586/tosc.v2024.i4.138-190; experimental output at github.com/IAIK/six-worlds-anemoi commit fa056e6f, read 2026-11-06
program.redistribution: the paper is open access and the experimental output is MIT, so its data may be redistributed; the committed CICO witnesses cite the results file they were extracted from

reference_points.hardware: Intel Xeon E5-2630 v3 @ 2.40 GHz, 378 GB, Debian 11

verifier: Anemoi::is_cico_solution runs the permutation on (0, y) and checks that the first output word is zero, so the check goes through the permutation rather than through the polynomial system - independent of the model and of every transformation applied to it. The reference's own check_polynomial_verification is the designers' equivalent and needs Sage; docs/research/anemoi.md section 4 records what was used instead.
notes: The same system over 2^32 - 209, the sweep's 32-bit prime. Registered for #283, to separate field arithmetic from conversion algorithmics: the reference's published conversion cost here is within 7% of its cost at 2^64 - 353 while its basis step is comparable, so a within-implementation ratio that moves between these two primes is about arithmetic and not about N. The sweep stops after the basis step at N = 5, so N = 6 here has no published figure for either step. As at 2^64 - 353, a result here says nothing about full-round Anemoi.
